## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 19 user-facing changes.
### New
- Click the Space in a Quick Window’s address bar to switch Spaces. The page reloads in the Space you choose, with that Space’s cookies and passwords, and Crest remembers the choice for that site. - Finished downloads can be dragged out of the Downloads list and dropped into Finder or another app, like any file. - Right-click the lists button at the bottom of the sidebar to choose whether it opens Archive, History or Downloads in the Space you are in. - Site Controls can clear the open site's cookies or its cache. Clearing cookies signs you out of the site and removes everything it stored in that Space, including service workers and what sites embedded in it stored there. Both are also in the command palette and, on iPhone and iPad, the page menu. - Each Space's Privacy settings list the sites that keep data, with Remove and Remove All, and can clear history, cookies and site data, and cached files from the last hour up to all time.
### Improved
- Pressing Command-T while the command bar is open closes it. - The floating sidebar stays open when the pointer drifts just past its edge, and hides once the pointer moves further into the page.
### Fixed
- Imported passwords for sites at an IP address written in a long or unusual form, such as 127.1, now fill on that site and merge with passwords already saved for it. - Pressing Shift-Return in Find moves to the previous match. - On iPad with a keyboard, pressing Tab in a webpage's form no longer switches to another Space. - Dragging across a Quick Window’s address field selects its text instead of moving the window. The space around the field still moves the window. - On a Start Page, Command-T closes an open command bar and puts the cursor back in the Start Page field.
---

## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 57 user-facing changes.
### New
- On iPhone and iPad, a swipe to go back or forward can also start on the frame around the page, where a finger reaching for the edge of the screen lands. - On iPhone, swiping left or right on the address bar moves through the tabs of your Space in sidebar order, and the page slides along with your finger. In a Split View, the other cards sit beside the address bar, and the swipe moves card by card before carrying on to the next tab. - Crest 0.8.50 updates Chromium with its latest security fixes and stops trusting the compromised eMudhra certificate authorities, rebuilds setup on the Mac, translates whole pages in Chromium, and fixes several crashes and problems quitting.
### Improved
- On iPad and iPhone Duo, the sidebar starts narrower, leaving more of the window to the page.
### Fixed
- On iPhone and iPad, Crest no longer leaves an empty band at the bottom of the window for a keyboard that isn't on screen. - On iPhone Duo, opening or closing the phone keeps the sidebar and its colors on the Space you're in instead of showing your first Space. - On iPhone Duo, a Split View made on the outer display shows both of its pages when you open the phone, instead of one staying blank until you tap it. - On iPhone and iPad, a Quick Window no longer leaves an empty band above it, and on iPad a Quick Window or Peek beside the sidebar stays on screen instead of running off its edge. - On iPhone and in a Mac Quick Window, leaving the address bar without going anywhere, by tapping or clicking away or pressing Escape, puts the page's address back instead of what you typed. - On iPad and iPhone Duo, the sidebar's tabs scroll on to the bottom of the screen and into its corner instead of stopping short above it. - Chromium is updated to 155.0.8059.84 with upstream security and compatibility fixes. - Pages that run in Chromium no longer trust certificates from the compromised eMudhra certificate authorities, matching Chrome.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
